name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 15 points
Austin Scott's ~$1.3 million cash advantage versus challenger's under $2,000
Incumbent seeking re-election with no outside spending in the race
Prediction markets price Scott's win probability near 98 percent
model.rationale: The R+15 district, Scott's incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly 60-to-1 leave Democrat Kelly Esti with no visible path, and prediction markets price Scott's chances near 98 percent.
model.watch: Any late infusion of Democratic outside spending or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would be the first sign of movement, though nothing currently points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Austin Scott, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win another term representing this south Georgia district, which leans Republican by about fifteen points. No general-election polling is available, but prediction markets give Scott roughly a 98 percent chance of victory, and no outside groups are spending meaningfully on either side.

The financial picture underscores the imbalance: Scott has raised about $1.1 million and holds $1.3 million on hand, while Kelly Esti, the Democratic challenger, has raised under $20,000 and had less than $2,000 remaining. With no expert ratings or polls suggesting a competitive race, this seat sits firmly in the Safe Republican column.
